Garry Tonon/Breaking Legs and Breaking H.overview: Garry Tonon's leg lock system in seven volumes (about 6 hours), from one of the original Danaher Death Squad members. Volume 1 introduces leg entanglements and breaking mechanics. Volume 2 covers irimi (standard) ashi garami, control and kuzushi. Volume 3 covers entries, mostly from seated guard and hand fighting. Volume 4 covers outside ashi and advanced breaking mechanics. Volume 5 covers cross ashi attacks and dragging entries. Volume 6 covers elevation entries (reverse X, sumi gaeshi). Volume 7 covers 50/50 and far-hip ashi.
Garry Tonon/Breaking Legs and Breaking H.for: No-gi grapplers wanting a full DDS-style leg lock education from a top competitor.

Garry Tonon/Exit The System.overview: Garry Tonon's escapes from the Danaher Death Squad submission systems, one per volume (about 5 hours across eight volumes). Volume 1 covers why to study escapes and how to train them. Then: kimura (prevention from top and bottom, escapes), guillotine (low and high elbow, early and late escapes), triangles (preventing front and reverse triangles, intercepting the legs, escapes), kata gatame / darce / anaconda, heel hooks (standard and outside ashi), toe holds (single leg and 'double trouble') and the omoplata (knee wedge, step over and others).
Garry Tonon/Exit The System.for: No-gi grapplers who want to be hard to submit.
key: Heel hook, toe hold and omoplata escapes

Garry Tonon/Shoot To Kill Wrestle, Scram.overview: Garry Tonon's submission-grappling takedown system in eight volumes (about 5.5 hours), mixing wrestling with ashi garami, front headlocks and back takes. Volume 1 covers posture and momentum (pushing, pulling, circular). Volume 2 covers the single leg and kosoto finishes. Volume 3 covers attacking the legs, including ashi garami pulls. Volume 4 covers ties (Victor's roll, collar tie, overhook). Volume 5 covers attacking the upper body with the front headlock. Volume 6 covers kata gatame, the cradle and 4-point. Volume 7 covers scrambles (Granby rolls and others). Volume 8 covers live drills and rolling.
Garry Tonon/Shoot To Kill Wrestle, Scram.for: No-gi competitors who want to start on the feet with a plan.

Garry Tonon/Unifying The Systems Navigat.overview: Garry Tonon shows how to move between the DDS submission systems so a defence to one attack opens another (eight volumes, about 6 hours). Volume 1 covers leg lock connections. Volume 2 covers back attacks (cross body ride, back to armbar). Volumes 3 and 4 cover the kimura (to front headlock, to the back, T-kimura from top and bottom). Volume 5 covers the front headlock (kata gatame and guillotine). Volume 6 covers armlocks. Volume 7 covers triangles. Volume 8 covers attacking in chains of three and four submissions.
Garry Tonon/Unifying The Systems Navigat.for: Intermediate-advanced no-gi players who know the individual systems and want to connect them.

Garry Tonon Fundamentals - Simple System.overview: Garry Tonon's fundamentals course built around small, simple systems (chains of 3-4 linked moves) for each phase of a match, in eight parts (about 6 hours). Part 1 covers an offensive system (double leg, Barzegar to armbar). Part 2 covers a defensive system (side control to stand-up, mount to sumi gaeshi). Part 3 covers back take systems (snaps with the whizzer and underhook). Part 4 covers sweeping systems (sumi gaeshi, knee lever). Part 5 covers back defence (hook sides, roll-throughs). Part 6 covers takedown systems (single leg, cross trip, high crotch). Part 7 covers passing systems (distance passing, knee slide). Part 8 covers early and late takedown defence.
Garry Tonon Fundamentals - Simple System.for: Beginners and intermediates who want a simple, connected game.

Get The Fuck Off Me Back Escapes by Etha.overview: B-Team member and ADCC veteran Ethan Crelinsten's back defence system in seven volumes (about 3.5 hours). Volume 1 covers basic objectives and 'strangle territory'. Volume 2 covers gauging danger (early, mid, late) and the belly-down escape. Volume 3 covers the turning escape and how to start it (shoulder slip, collarbone misalignment). Volume 4 covers the classic back positions (seatbelt without hooks, overhook side, two hooks). Volume 5 covers defending arm switches and timing hip posts. Volume 6 covers breaking the mount cycle and not letting their weight settle. Volume 7 covers live back situations with commentary.
Get The Fuck Off Me Back Escapes by Etha.for: Anyone whose back gets taken; especially useful for no-gi and submission-only (EBI overtime) players.
key: Escaping each seatbelt and hook configuration
